definition: Captive multinational legal subsidiaries with primary engineering, R&D, product, or digital shared-services mandates in India. Excludes third-party IT/BPM outsourcers and staffing vendors.
whyItDiffers: Entity-level consolidation: a single multinational (e.g., Microsoft or JPMorgan) is counted as exactly 1 GCC entity regardless of how many cities or campuses it operates across.

source: Zinnov-NASSCOM India GCC Landscape Report 2026 (Units Metric)
definition: Total physical operational campuses and centers across cities. The average Indian GCC now runs from nearly 1.8 to 2 cities rather than one.
whyItDiffers: Measures physical real estate footprint: 2,117 distinct corporate entities operate across 3,728 physical units nationwide (Bengaluru: 29%+ share; NCR, Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai sharing remainder).

definition: Historical FY24 benchmark measuring incorporated captive multinational entities in India.
whyItDiffers: Baseline vintage: Over 417 net new GCC entities entered India between FY24 and FY26 as enterprise tech and AI mandates surged.

definition: Total physical operational campuses in FY24 across metro micro-markets.
whyItDiffers: Real estate units benchmark crossing 2,975 units for 1,700 entities in FY24.

definition: Counts active Employer-of-Record (EOR) / BOT 'pre-incorporation' units that function as dedicated GCCs under partner umbrellas alongside incorporated captives.
whyItDiffers: Broader boundary capturing companies in incubation or early growth phase before formal ROC incorporation.

definition: Informal rounded figure repeatedly cited in news articles, conflating corporate entities with active leases.
whyItDiffers: Journalistic shorthand that omits the technical distinction between 2,117 legal corporate entities and 3,728 physical units.
